subject: Post-call: CarePlus model-fit proofpack, perf snapshots & regression guardrails
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Ortiz <janelle@careplus.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: CarePlus model-fit proofpack, perf snapshots & regression guardrails

Hi Janelle —

Thanks again for the call today. Short recap and the items we promised to share so your infra and ML teams can validate fit for the CarePlus triage pilot.

Key takeaways (from our side):
- Goal: 2–3k concurrent active sessions for triage assistant, median request size ~120 tokens, ~60% of calls are short (<=40 tokens).
- Primary concerns you raised: hallucination rate on clinical notes, P99 latency under 350ms for single-turn queries, and predictable unit cost.

Redwood-recommended model slate (pilot candidates):
1) RedWeave-13B (fp16, standard): strong quality; best P95/P99 under typical sequence lengths; recommend for first-quality pass.
2) LlamaX-7B (q8_0): lower cost, good throughput; suitable for high-concurrency fallback and routing for low-risk templates.
3) OpenMed-30B (int8-pref): highest QA but requires capacity; consider for escalation paths / complex summarization.

Attached proofpack + quick links:
- Redwood-verified perf snapshots (TPS & latency percentiles) for the slate: https://app.redwood.ai/perf/benchmarks/redweave-13b-20281101
- Shared Drive: prompt sets, eval prompts, and regression checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bCarePlusProofpack
- Prompt set included: CarePlus_MVP_prompt_set_v1.json (attached)

Quick perf highlights (snapshots from our lab, median co-located infra):
- RedWeave-13B (fp16): TPS (single model) = 220 tok/s; latency p50=48ms, p95=192ms, p99=310ms at 8 concurrent streams.
- LlamaX-7B (q8): TPS = 480 tok/s; latency p50=22ms, p95=95ms, p99=180ms at 32 concurrent streams.
- OpenMed-30B (int8): TPS = 95 tok/s; latency p50=120ms, p95=410ms, p99=720ms at 4 concurrent streams.

Notes on regression risk and guardrails:
- Hallucination/watchlist: we recommend active quality monitors (prompt-based invariants + entity-level F1 checks) and scheduled evals on your golden prompt set (we included a 120-prompt starting pack).
- Routing: use RedWeave for primary answers; fall back to LlamaX for cost-constrained requests and to OpenMed for high-risk / escalation paths.
- Caching: KV-prefix caching expected to cut token cost by ~12–18% for repeated templates.

Next steps / asks from CarePlus to proceed with pilot:
1) Confirm pilot scope (sample size, redaction policy for PHI preview data).
2) Share an S3 link or staging dataset (anonymized) with 500 representative interactions.
3) Approve pilot config (we propose: RedWeave-13B primary, LlamaX fallback, 3-day rolling eval cadence).
4) Book kickoff for week of Nov 13 — 30-minute technical alignment + infra checklist.

Attachments: CarePlus_MVP_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt pack), perf_snapshot_redweave_13b.pdf (snapshot).

—
Irene Choi
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: CarePlus model-fit proofpack, perf snapshots & regression guardrails

Thanks, Irene — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our engineering lead (cc'd in our internal thread):

- For the TPS numbers you reported, are those steady-state with Redwood batching enabled? What concurrency per-GPU were those measured at?
- Our latency SLO is 200ms for the single-turn UX path — do we have a configuration of RedWeave that meets that at our target concurrency (2–3k active users)?
- Hallucination: can you share a short example of the entity-level checks you mentioned? We need something we can plug into our automated regression pipeline.

Also, curious if you have a recommended pilot duration and a minimal success threshold (e.g., <2% entity hallucination on the 120-prompt set and p95 < 350ms). We can start anonymizing a small sample this week.

Thanks —
Janelle

janelle@careplus.ai

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Ortiz <janelle@careplus.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Nov 2028 14:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: CarePlus model-fit proofpack, perf snapshots & regression guardrails

Hi Janelle — quick answers and a proposed pilot config. Quoting parts of Irene's note below for context.

> For the TPS numbers you reported, are those steady-state with Redwood batching enabled? What concurrency per-GPU were those measured at?

Yes — the numbers Irene shared were measured with Redwood continuous batching on (latency-aware batching) and our standard kernel selection. Single GPU concurrency assumptions:
- RedWeave-13B: tested at 8 streams / GPU (fp16); recommended pool of 4 GPUs to start the pilot (~1750 effective TPS aggregate for the primary slice).
- LlamaX-7B: tested at 32 streams / GPU (q8); excellent density — plan for 4–6 GPUs if you route ~60% of traffic there as fallback.

To hit the 2–3k active session target while keeping p95 < 350ms we recommend:
- Pilot baseline: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for RedWeave + 3x for LlamaX fallback (autoscale up to 6x RedWeave if warmup shows quality needs).
- Config: batching window = 12ms (adaptive), KV cache TTL = 60s for session-level caching, quant profile = fp16 primary / q8 fallback for cost tiering.

Entity-level regression checks (examples you can run on nightly eval):
- Named Entity Stabilizer: for clinical entities (diagnosis codes, medication names), compute token-level precision/recall against golden labels; flag sessions where F1 drops >3 pts.
- Consistency invariants: if user asks a factual numeric question answered earlier in the session, answer must not contradict a prior canonical field (simple fuzzy-match + date tolerance).
- Hallucination detector: prompt-based filter that asks model to list sources / cite spans; if no overlapping source tokens found, flag for human review.

Proposed success thresholds for pilot (starting point):
- Quality: entity-level hallucinations < 2.5% on the 120-prompt set
- Latency: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for triage flow
- Ops: no more than 2 unplanned escalations to SRE per week during steady-state

Next steps I can action this week if you confirm:
1) We publish a tailored perf snapshot for your anonymized sample (we'll need S3 access).
2) I'll create a short Runbook + Canary checklist and link it to the HubSpot deal record: https://hubspot.com/contacts/Deal-RW-CP-2028-11
3) Schedule technical kickoff (Irene / Monica / infra) — propose Nov 14 at 09:00 PT or Nov 15 at 11:00 PT.

—Michael
Director, Inference Ops, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai
